title: Full English Breakfast
subtitle: The complete fry-up
excerpt: Bacon, sausages, fried eggs, baked beans, grilled tomatoes, and black pudding. The timing and order of cooking is what makes a good fry-up, not any single element.

recipe.sourceNotes: The full English breakfast as we know it developed in the Victorian era, with the cooked breakfast becoming a social institution of the professional and middle classes. The standard components varied by region but typically include bacon, eggs, sausages, and toast.

recipeTools.notes: A large pan to fit the bacon and sausages.
A second pan for the eggs.

content.text: A full English breakfast is a matter of timing. The sausages take longest, so they go in first. The bacon and black pudding need the hot fat the sausages leave behind. The tomatoes and beans run alongside. The eggs go in last and are done in minutes. Everything should be ready at once and served on a warm plate.

Warm the plates in a low oven at 100 C. Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the sausages for 12 to 15 minutes, turning regularly, until deep brown all over and cooked through.

While the sausages cook, put the baked beans in a small saucepan over a low heat and warm gently. Place the tomato halves cut-side up under a medium grill. Season and grill for 8 to 10 minutes until soft.

Move the cooked sausages to the warm oven. In the same pan with the sausage fat, fry the bacon for 2 to 3 minutes per side until it reaches your preferred crispness. Add the black pudding for the last 2 minutes, turning once. Transfer to the oven to keep warm.
Add the butter to the pan. When foaming, crack in the eggs and fry over a medium-low heat until the whites are just set and the yolks are still runny.
Put the bread in the toaster. Arrange everything on the warm plates and serve immediately.
